scenario: AITA for not wanting to attend my great aunt's funeral? | So today I came home from college (Britain, so American High School, I think). The second I walk through the door my mum tells me that her grandma's sister has died. "Your great aunt Wyn died and the funeral will probably be soon." My first thoughts were 'Who?' and 'Why is she telling me this?' I have actually never heard this name before or met this person besides the one time I found out today I had met her when I was still extremely young and unable to walk for myself. This turned into a slight argument as, for some reason, she wanted me to go this funeral, despite knowing I am a really awkward person at funeral's for people I've met more than once, let along a funeral for someone I've met only once and have no idea who is part of the family. The argument ends with her trying to guilt-trip me by outright just saying "Fine, I'll go on my own." in a really sulky way. Her only arguments for me going were that I'd be going out of 'respect' and support for her, despite that she has never once mentioned this great aunt to me even though she supposedly played a massive hand in raising her as my grandmother, and that it's one of the few times we'll see the much larger branch of the family where it's likely to be a few hundred of us, about 10 of which I have seen more than once but still at most 10 times, maybe not even that. To me, it would feel like gatecrashing the funeral for someone else's family and that, even though I am part of the family, no one would want me there since I do not know nor did I know the person who died. I don't know how much this takes precedence over everything else but it felt like it had to reiterated a lot - I have never met this person besides the one time she met me when I was either 1 or 2 years old and the name has never been mentioned to me before now, at least not to my recollection. So, AITA for not wanting to attend someone who is practically a stranger to me's wedding for the sole reason that she's family?

First, I came home from college in Britain, which is like an American high school, I think. My mom told me that my great aunt Wyndy died, and the funeral will probably be soon. My initial thoughts were confusion because I didn't know who she was. I've never heard her name before, and the only time I met her was when I was extremely young, maybe 1 or 2 years old. So, I don't really have any memories or connection to her. My mom wanted me to go to the funeral, but I feel really awkward at funerals, especially for people I don't know well. I mean, I'm already anxious at funerals for people I know, so going to one for someone I barely met once seems really strange. My mom tried to guilt-trip me into going, saying I should go out of respect and support for her. But I'm confused because she's never mentioned this great aunt before, even though she supposedly played a big role in raising her. That makes me question why she's bringing this up now. I also thought about the family aspect. The funeral would be a chance to meet a larger branch of the family, maybe hundreds of people, but I've only seen about 10 of them more than once. It feels like gate-crashing someone else's family event. I don't know if anyone would even want me there since I don't know the person who died or much about her. From a Christian perspective, I'm thinking about what the Bible says about family and respect. The Bible does talk about honoring parents and family, but it also emphasizes love and support. However, I'm not sure if attending a funeral for someone I don't know counts as honoring family. I feel like my mom is asking me to do something that doesn't make sense to me, and I'm not sure if it's a sin to not go. I also wonder about the practical aspects. Would going to the funeral help me connect with my family more? Or would it just make me uncomfortable and stressed? I don't want to cause more problems by not going, but I also don't want to force myself into a situation that doesn't feel right. Maybe I should talk to my mom about my feelings and see if we can find a middle ground. Perhaps there's another way to show respect without attending the funeral. But I'm not sure how she'll react. She might feel hurt or think I'm being disrespectful, which I don't want. In the end, I'm torn between respecting my family's wishes and honoring my own feelings and comfort. I need to decide what's more important in this situation and how to handle it in a way that aligns with my Christian values.
